notes.1i: Most candidates gained at least partial credit for giving the correct orders with respect to reactants but some did not refer to data in table, as required by the question.
notes.1ii: Many candidates carried out the calculation correctly, although many ignored the need for two significant figures, as required by the question.
notes.1iii: Most candidates were able to give a correct equation.
notes.1iv: Many candidates carried out the calculation correctly giving the correct units of k. A common error was k being calculated using incorrect experimental data.
notes.1b: Most candidates gained at least partial credit here, though the shape and clarity of many curves needed to be improved. Many candidates needed to be more precise with their explanations.
notes.1c: Many candidates did not realise that the orders suggested that one molecule of F2 and one molecule of NO were involved in the rate determining slow step.
notes.2a: This question was not well answered, with many candidates not applying the rules of orbital occupancy for the nickel atom. For the formation of the ion, some candidates incorrectly removed d electrons.
notes.2i: Many candidates gave the correct answer here.
notes.2ii: There were some good answers, although many candidates did not recall that lower energy d orbitals have each of the lobes pointing between two of the axes or that higher energy d orbitals have their lobes pointing along the axes.
notes.2c: Most candidates gained credit here. Some candidates did not describe the promotion of an electron from a lower to a higher level by the absorption of visible light, or the colour transmitted (not emitted) being the complement of the colour absorbed.
notes.2d: Many candidates gained partial credit here using their knowledge of Cu chemistry to answer this question. A was Ni(OH)2 and both 4-coordinated and six-coordinated complexes of B were credited. A common error was unbalanced equations.
notes.3i: Most candidates gave the correct definition of the lattice energy. Weaker answers involved the description of a mole of ionic compound being formed from 1 mole of its gaseous ions.
notes.3ii: Many candidates managed to suggest a valid reason here.
notes.4i: This was generally well answered, although there were many incorrect or unbalanced equations.
notes.4ii: The explanation required here should have been learnt. Whilst the majority of candidates knew that ethanoic acid was less acidic than chloroethanoic acid, and that ethanol was less acidic than phenol, many did not relate these acidities to valid explanations.
notes.4c: Many candidates seemed unable to draw upon knowledge from a range of areas of the organic chemistry syllabus here. The type of reaction with Na and the reaction with hot excess NaOH
notes.5a: Candidates should be aware of the relative rate of hydrolysis of these organohalogen compounds. Although some candidates gave the correct order of hydrolysis, the explanation in terms of C-Cl bond strength was not always given.
notes.5b: Most candidates identified the correct functional groups here but should note that vague terms such as carbonyl or carboxylic are not detailed enough for credit to be awarded.
notes.5i: Again, candidates need to be sure of the methods used for drawing curly arrows in such a reaction mechanism.
notes.5ii: Many candidates were able to give the correct mechanism.
notes.5iii: Most candidates correctly identified HBr. However CH3Br was a common incorrect answer.
notes.5d: Most candidates gained at least partial credit here. W and Y were more commonly correct than X. Candidates need to take care when drawing structures to avoid mistakes. X was often incorrectly drawn as an ester.
notes.5e: Candidates should be reminded to read the question. Here they were asked to give two repeat units; this was very often not seen.

notes.6d: Many candidates answered this question well.

notes.7b: Many candidates were able to give a correct answer here.

notes.8i: Some candidates managed to correctly identify the structure of T. Many incorrectly suggested butan-2-ol.
notes.8iii: Most candidates gained at least partial credit here. notes.key_messages: Candidates are reminded to read questions carefully and check answers thoroughly. In this paper, candidates would have benefitted from this particularly in Questions 1(d)(ii), 1(d)(iv), 2(b)(ii), 4(a) and 4(c), where answers frequently included unbalanced equations or, in some cases, no equations at all. Candidates need to ensure that all equations given are balanced and are also reminded that their working in calculations should be shown to ensure that due credit can be awarded. This was especially important in Question 2(d)(iii).
notes.general_comments: General Comments This examination paper provided a difficult challenge to the candidates with some pleasing performances. Ten questions can be said to have been found to be easier. 50% or more of candidates chose the correct responses to each of Questions 8, 9, 11, 13, 20, 22, 28, 29, 33 and 35. Questions 38 and 39 were also answered correctly by a high proportion of candidates, suggesting they had sufficient time. Seven questions can be said to have been found to be particularly difficult. Fewer than 25% of candidates chose the correct responses to each of Questions 4, 6, 10, 24, 25, 37 and 40. Comments on Specific Questions
